**STEP 1 - Scene:** A single slice of toast spread with red jam (looks like strawberry jam), on a white square plate. It is photographed from directly above. The bowl of strawberries at the left edge is on a separate dish, so I excluded it.

**STEP 2 - Ruler:** The plate is about 22 cm across. Area = 3.14 × (11)² ≈ 380 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) toast bread slice, (2) strawberry jam spread over the top.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The slice covers about 160 cm², roughly 42% of the plate. Jam covers most of the slice top, about 130 cm², roughly 34% of the plate. Food covers about 42% of the plate in total.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Bread is about 1 cm thick, so 160 cm² × 1 cm ≈ 160 ml of envelope. Jam is a thin layer, about 130 cm² × 0.3 cm ≈ 39 ml.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** A toast slice is a light, aerated item, so I use the bread-slice estimate of about 35 g, which is in line with a typical slice rather than the 0.9 density the table gives for dense bread. Jam is about 20 g, since a thin spread is much less than the 39 ml envelope suggests.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Toast at about 250 kcal/100 g gives 35 g ≈ 88 kcal. Strawberry jam at about 260 kcal/100 g gives 20 g ≈ 52 kcal. Total ≈ 55 g, ≈ 140 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** One slice of jam toast is typically 40–60 g and 130–170 kcal, so these numbers are plausible for what is visible.
